children: Entain said it plans to cut around 400 jobs across several locations as the company grapples with the impact of higher U.K. gambling taxes.

The sports-betting and gambling group, which houses British brands Ladbrokes and Coral, said Wednesday that it would start a consultation process that could lead to the removal of around 400 of its 2,000 customer service roles.
The announcement comes days before the company's exit from the FTSE 100 index takes effect.

"The proposed changes are being made to ensure our business remains competitive, financially resilient, and well positioned for the future as our sector faces an increasingly challenging operating environment," Chief Executive Officer Stella David said.
Earlier this year, Entain said it expects to offset more than half of the higher U.K. tax burden through optimization efforts from 2027.

In November, the British government outlined its plans to raise its remote-gaming duty to 40% from 21% from April 2026. Meanwhile, the new duty rate of 25% for remote betting will apply to profits from remote betting from April 2027.
In early European afternoon trading, London-listed shares were down 0.1% at 497.80 pence, having fallen to a low of 487.0 pence earlier in the session.

"Job cuts normally fire up a share price, but not in this case. Sentiment remains weak towards Entain as it loses momentum in a highly competitive sector," AJ Bell's Russ Mould wrote in a note to clients.
Entain employs more than 28,000 people globally, according to its website.
